summary_plain:
I checked the design for shortcuts and leaks. Shortcut here means a simple rule that learns nothing yet still scores well. Leak here means test answers reaching the builder. I recomputed every fact myself with plain Python. I ran no model.

What holds up: the bank facts in A1 are correct. The frozen bank has 64 worlds and 6 shapes, with 12/12/12/12/8/8 worlds per shape, and each shape appears in all 4 domains. A shape is a pattern of "contains" arrows, ignoring names. Counting every connected shape with no loops gives 4, 24 and 267 at 3, 4 and 5 nodes. So the design's new-shape counts of 3, 19 and 267 are right. All of that is MEASURED.

What breaks, in plain words:

(1) At 3 and 4 nodes, a no-learning rule that just counts arrows in and out of each node already solves analogy and correspondence. Analogy asks which other-domain world has the same shape. Correspondence asks which node matches which. Among all 28 shapes, only one pair shares the same counts. So the bar is about 1.0. Even a perfect model cannot beat it, and a win would not show it read structure. The power sums assume a bar of 0.25. The bar for correspondence is at least 0.50, because half its items have "no match" as the answer.

(2) The reach-VIA test counts only questions whose true answer is VIA. VIA means the part is reached through an in-between node. The design's bar rules score 0 to 0.22 there. A rule that always says "VIA through the whole's alphabetically first child" gets 348/384 = 0.906 on the new 4-node shapes. So a label-order shortcut would pass.

(3) The "sealed" test shapes are not sealed. There are only 22 new shapes at 3 and 4 nodes, and anyone can list them. The builder gets the 11 development shapes, so the other 11 are the test shapes. Helm never reads node names, so hiding the names protects almost nothing.

(4) Only 14 structurally different VIA questions exist across all 22 new shapes. So "80 test questions" are really about 7 questions, each renamed many times. The p-values overstate the evidence.

(5) The wiring probe passes a repair that adds the same number to every candidate's score. That repair can never change which world is picked. I confirmed this by replaying the probe's verdict arithmetic on a made-up scorer. It read PRESENT with 0 top-choice changes out of 140 rewirings.

(6) The frozen checker refuses graphs above 4 nodes. So the 5-node analogy and correspondence cells cannot be scored as written. Also, one 5-node world in the 64-world bank would break every analogy question that uses that bank.

(7) In the bank, the "participant" marks already give a correct node matching in 640 of 640 same-shape pairs. Helm reads these marks. The design does not say how new worlds will set them.

Smaller issues: there is no comparator that ignores the focus world, and Helm 2.0 is exactly that kind of model. The fresh-word rule and the domain words conflict. The Q4 "new structure" readout uses a split the builder can already see.

findings.problem: At 3-4 nodes (NEW_SHAPE_SAME_SIZE, the primary transfer cell), the registered degree-multiset comparator is effectively exact for analogy and for correspondence match/no-match, and simple degree-signature matching nearly always gives a valid bijection. So the bar for analogy and correspondence is about 1.0. Under A7 (b > c with p <= 0.01), even a perfect model ties at b = 0 and can never read BEATS_NO_LEARNING_BAR. And because Helm gets in/out degree as direct node inputs, a 'win' could not tell structure-reading from degree-counting anyway. A5's power figures assume a 0.25 comparator. That is wrong for these families: the constant NO_MATCH comparator alone scores 0.50 on correspondence, because A4 makes half its items NO_MATCH.

Of the 22 new same-size shapes, 21 have a unique (in,out)-degree multiset.
MEASURED: for 20/22 new same-size shapes, EVERY degree-signature-preserving bijection is a valid isomorphism (3/3 at 3 nodes, 17/19 at 4 nodes). Four-round colour refinement (WL) gives 22/22.

findings.problem: The reach primary cell is scored on VIA-gold questions only, and none of the registered comparators is a VIA-biased label-order rule. On a VIA-only cell: constant ABSENT scores 0; the one-hop rule (DIRECT iff child, else not VIA) scores 0; rank-last scores about 0.22. But 'if no direct edge, answer VIA through the lowest-rank (alphabetically first) child of the whole' needs no path search and scores about 0.91. The lexical tie-break in first_direct_constituent_lexical_v1 is what makes this rule match the gold so often. A model that learned 'never ABSENT, take the first child' would be certified BEATS_NO_LEARNING_BAR on reach-VIA.

findings.problem: The wiring probe's PRESENT verdict is met by a repair that adds the same focus-dependent constant to every candidate world's score. Such a shift cannot change which world is chosen, so it cannot fix the A7 witness failure (a fixed candidate ranking). Yet it satisfies M1 > 1e-4 and 90% of M3 > 1e-4, because the probe measures absolute score change per candidate, not change relative to the other candidates. Top-1 change is reported but excluded from the verdict. B1 is the stated prerequisite for reading any analogy cell, so the gate can certify the wrong thing.

summary_plain:
Short version: the probe can tell "no wire at all" apart from "some wire". It cannot yet tell a real comparison apart from a fake one.

What is right. On the unchanged Helm 2.0, the probe's prediction of ABSENT follows from the code. Every one of the 70 analogy records carries all 64 worlds and has an empty argument list. Each world is encoded on its own, and the focus world only sets its own flag. The exact-zero threshold (1e-6) suits that case. The worry that a repair could pass through the focus candidate itself, or through the world count, does not hold: the probe leaves the focus candidate out, and the world count is the same in every record.

What is wrong, most serious first.

1. The known issue is confirmed by measurement. I fed the probe's own verdict code synthetic scores of the form "focus-dependent shift + focus-dependent scale × a fixed candidate score". That is a repair with no comparison at all. The probe returned PRESENT (M1 = 0.4901 or 2.5115; 100% of records above the threshold). Yet 0 of 248 rewirings changed the order of the other candidates, and 0 changed the top pick. The judge A7's finding is about ORDER: a fixed ranking cannot pick from two separate answer sets. The probe measures raw score change, not order, so it can certify the very thing A7 ruled out.

2. The "switch OFF must reproduce the before-reading exactly" check does not test preservation. For a model with no focus dependency, M1, M2 and M3 are 0 whatever the scores are, and the probe never saves the scores themselves. A switch-OFF model whose scores all changed would still pass.

3. Two other non-comparison routes also pass:
   - A shared coupling across all worlds, such as normalising across candidates. There is no control that rewires a non-focus world.
   - Random noise or non-repeatable GPU operations. There is no repeat run to measure the noise floor.

4. The rewiring does not reach every copy of the focus graph. The reading keeps a second copy in `reading["focus_world"]`, and the probe edits only `reading["worlds"][focus]`.

5. The probe runs only on freshly built models. A new part that starts at zero, as Helm's own `round_rate` does, would read ABSENT even when the repair is correct. And a trained model that learned to switch the path off would never be checked.

6. NO_MATCH is left out, but it is a real answer option with a fixed score of 0. In 32 of the 248 rewirings the correct answer becomes NO_MATCH. About 25% of HSET-1 analogy items are NO_MATCH.

7. The focus world's domain is never changed, although A7's repair order names both graph and domain. Both witness records are in the grammatical domain.

8. Smaller points:
   - The prereg says the other arrangements come from the bank. The code adds 2 made-up 3-node shapes, which may fall in the sealed test pool.
   - The 90% rule counts records (70), not distinct focus worlds (24).
   - The reported top-pick diagnostic does not follow the model's real decision rule.

Proposed fix, in outline:
- Standardise each record's candidate scores (subtract the mean, divide by the spread).
- Add a rank-change measure and an answer-set contrast.
- Add a rewire of a non-focus world as a control, a repeat-run noise gate, a NO_MATCH margin, and a domain swap.
- Add a byte-level digest of all scores for the switch-OFF preservation check.
- Run the probe on trained repaired checkpoints too, not only fresh models.
Exact thresholds are in the findings below.

Claim states:
- Measured: F1's synthetic replay, and the counts 70 / 24 / 248 / 32.
- Read from the code: F2, F4 and the rewiring mechanics.
- Inferred: that global-coupling and noise paths would pass (F3).
- Nothing was run on a GPU. Torch was not imported.

findings.fix: Replace raw M1/M3 by per-record standardised scores over the cross-domain non-focus candidates X (only they can be answers): z_c=(s_c-mean_X s)/sd_X s. M3z(r)=max over rewires of max_{c in X}|Δz_c|; K(r)=max over rewires of Kendall discordant-pair fraction on X; RC(r)=mean over rewires S->S' of |mean_{A'}Δz - mean_{A}Δz| where A/A' are the cross-domain isomorphs of the old/new focus shape (the old and new accepted sets). M1z = max_{c shared}|z_c(a)-z_c(b)|. PRESENT requires, on >=22 of the 24 distinct focus worlds: M3z >= 1e-2, K > 0 on at least one rewire, and median RC >= 1e-2; plus M1z >= 1e-2. Affine-in-focus transforms give M3z=K=RC=0 exactly and therefore cannot pass.

findings.problem: 'Switch OFF must reproduce the before-reading exactly' does not test preservation. The before-reading is ABSENT with M1=M2=M3=0; for any model without focus dependency those numbers are 0 whatever its scores are, and the probe never writes the scores. A switch-OFF build that changed every logit (a changed init RNG stream, a changed LayerNorm, an extra term) still reproduces the verdict and the zero M-values. Also 'identical' is undefined: the output JSON necessarily differs in source_sha256_lf (the repair edits pointer_learner.py), timings and GPU telemetry. The design relies on this check (EVALUATION_DESIGN_v0_1.md:191).

findings.problem: Two further non-comparison routes pass PRESENT. (a) A global coupling across worlds, such as normalising or softmax-pooling world vectors across all 64 candidates, or any batched op whose statistics include the focus world. Rewiring the focus then moves every candidate's score, including their order, with no pairwise focus-to-candidate comparison. The probe has no control that separates this from a comparison. (b) A noise path: non-repeatable CUDA ops (atomic scatter/index_add message passing) or stray stochastic ops. With tau_present=1e-4 in absolute logits, reduction-order noise alone can exceed the bar. The probe never repeats a forward pass, and it does not set the deterministic/TF32 flags the training worker sets.

findings.fix: (i) M0 noise gate: set the worker's flags plus CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG, run every base forward twice, and require δ0 = max|s-s'| <= 1e-6, else the verdict is INVALID_NONDETERMINISTIC. Every PRESENT effect must also be >= 100×δ0. (ii) M4 third-party leakage control: apply the same rewirings to one non-focus world c' (for example the lexically first cross-domain world of the focus's size), and measure L(r)=max_{c in X\{c'}}|Δz_c|. A pairwise comparison predicts L≈0. Require median over foci of M3z/L >= 10, and report L raw. (iii) Add a same-shape control: permute the focus world's node order and carry its node fields along. This must give M3z <= 1e-6, since the encoder has no rank feature (pointer_contract.py:896), which shows the effect comes from structure and not from node order.

findings.problem: The rewiring does not reach every copy of the focus graph in the reading. read_packet stores a second deep copy of the focus world in reading['focus_world'], including its 'contains'. The probe edits only reading['worlds'][focus]['contains'], so the counterfactual reading is internally inconsistent. The current learner never reads reading['focus_world'] (grep found no use), so the before-reading is unaffected. But a repair that takes 'the arrangement Helm is asked to compare' from the natural field reading['focus_world'] would see the stale graph: M3 would read 0 and a correct repair would be scored MIXED or ABSENT. The cached plan (slots.compile_slots) and input digest are also not rebuilt.

summary_plain:
I reviewed the design, the probe rules and the probe code. I read the Helm source files: source.py, answers.py, slots.py, checker.py, pointer_inputs.py, pointer_learner.py and course.py. I checked the numbers with pure-Python scripts only: no torch, no model, no sealed or eval file. Scratch files are in C:/Users/wakil/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-wakil-OneDrive-Desktop-tksCAS-cas-only-reasoner/5e8709f4-3151-444f-939b-317c01bc3568/scratchpad/hset_review/stats/.

These numbers check out:
- The bank has 64 worlds in 6 shapes (12/12/12/12/8/8), and each shape appears in all 4 domains.
- There are 3, 19 and 267 new shapes at 3, 4 and 5 nodes.
- The power figures are right: 30/80 gives power 0.9908, or 0.9728 over three runs. 24/60 gives 0.9538, or 0.8676. 40 questions gives 0.4841 over three runs.
- Part D's shape counts are right: 16 training shapes, 9 dev shapes, 0 shared, and 256 dev rows at depth 3.

The design still has serious problems:
1. The 5-node split cannot be scored for analogy or correspondence. The frozen checker stops at 4 nodes. If any 5-node world is in the bank, every analogy question fails to score. Fixing this means editing the checker, which is the answer path.
2. At 3 and 4 nodes, a no-learning rule that only counts arrows in and out of each node is almost perfect on analogy and correspondence. A perfect model can never beat it, so those two families can never pass.
3. The 11 sealed same-size shapes hold only about 7 distinct reach-VIA questions. So 80 items are mostly the same few questions repeated. The simple comparators never answer VIA, so a model that is right on 7 copies of one pattern passes the cell.
4. The sample-size calculation is for a different test from the success rule.
5. The sealed shapes are simply the 11 new shapes that are not in the development set, so the builder can work them out.
6. Helm reads two hints the design does not control: the participant rank and the declared whole. In the bank, the "participant 2" node is the VIA answer in 41 of 56 cases.
7. Using fresh declaration words sends the domain signal to rows of Helm's declaration table that were never trained.
8. The wiring probe can read PRESENT from a change that cannot reorder the candidates.
9. The wiring rule for a fresh model conflicts with starting both arms from the same weights.
10. Part D's "familiar" readout changes size from arm to arm. It is empty (0 rows) if an arm trains on all 2,048 rows.
11. Part C gives a shortened query id and no allowed tolerance, so it cannot be checked as written.

On Codex's questions: the reader and slot code accept a new bank of up to 64 worlds without edits, but correspondence stops at 4 nodes. The course generator does need a new external builder. That builder would not touch the answer path, but it must label test worlds with split "training".

findings.problem: NEW_SHAPE_LARGER (5-node) analogy and correspondence cells cannot be produced or scored with the frozen code. The frozen checker refuses any graph over 4 nodes. For analogy, it checks the whole bank first, so one 5-node world in the eval bank makes EVERY analogy question in that bank unscorable (TYPED_CHECKER_ISOMORPHISM_BOUND). The slot compiler also refuses correspondence over 4 nodes. There is a capacity problem too: 40 sealed 5-node shapes x at least 2 domains = 80 partner worlds, but the bank maximum is 64. Only reach, parts and edge_account work at 5 nodes. The fix would need edits to checker.py and answers.py, which are the answer path the design says stays frozen.

findings.fix: Drop analogy and correspondence from NEW_SHAPE_LARGER, or register a new checker version with its own name and profile digest. Either way, say plainly that A5's 'three splits' for these families is not buildable on the frozen checker. Keep 5-node questions for reach, parts and edge_account only. Never put a 5-node world into a bank that analogy is scored against.

findings.problem: The bar comparator, degree-multiset (a count of arrows in and out of each node), almost fully solves analogy and correspondence at 3-4 nodes. So a perfect learner cannot pass the A7 rule on NEW_SHAPE_SAME_SIZE for those two families: b stays near 0, and b >= 7 is needed when c = 0. At 3 nodes, the degree signature separates all 4 shapes. At 4 nodes it gives 23 classes for 24 shapes. The only collision is the new shape ((0,1),(0,2),(1,3),(3,2)) against the bank diamond. The correspondence degree rule, which picks the first degree-preserving map, scores 1.0 on all 3-node shapes and on 17 of 19 new 4-node shapes. It scores 0.5 on the other 2, for a mean of 0.9474. The degree rule does fail often at 5 nodes (105 of 267 shapes share a signature), but that is exactly where the checker cannot score (F1). As written, TRANSFERS_TO_NEW_STRUCTURE can only ever be earned by reach. It would print 'no transfer' for analogy and correspondence whatever the model does.

If it stays a bar, the analogy and correspondence items must be built where it fails: same node count, same edge count and same degree multiset, but not isomorphic. That needs 5+ nodes, which needs a new checker version (F1). Otherwise, state before any run that these two families can only earn 'matches the degree rule', never 'beats no-learning'.

findings.problem: There are too few distinct reach-VIA questions to fill 80 independent items, and the test treats repeats as independent. All 22 new 3-4-node shapes together carry only 14 non-tie VIA (whole, part) questions, plus 2 tie cases. 11 of the 22 shapes have none, and all three new 3-node shapes have none. Over all 705,432 possible 11/11 splits, the sealed half gets a median of 7 non-tie VIA questions from a median of 5 shapes. Its range is 1 to 13, and P(<=4) = 0.0885. FAMILIAR_RENAMED has only 6 labelled VIA questions in the 6 bank shapes (5 non-tie plus the diamond tie). So 80 VIA items means each structural question repeated about 11 times. The exact sign test treats every repeat as an independent coin. Constant ABSENT and the one-hop rule never output VIA, so the bar on a VIA cell is about 0. b = 7 with c = 0 gives p = 0.0078. So one learned structural pattern copied 7 or more times certifies BEATS_NO_LEARNING_BAR.

Score a cluster as correct only if all its instances and presentations are correct, then run the sign test over clusters. Alternatively use a cluster-level permutation test. Print the effective n for each cell. If there are fewer than about 10 clusters, say before any run that the cell cannot support a claim, or add VIA supply from 5-node shapes, where the checker's reach rule works.

findings.problem: Section A5 sizes the sample for one test, and A7 decides success with another. A5 uses a one-sample exact binomial against a fixed 0.25 chance level. A7 uses a paired sign test against the best comparator. In a sign test only the disagreeing pairs count, and 0.25 is the bar of no actual cell. On a VIA-only reach cell the bar is about 0, so 7/80 correct passes, not 30/80. On analogy and correspondence the bar is about 1.0, so nothing passes (F2). The composition is also unclear. A4 line 110 says reach is 'ABSENT / DIRECT / VIA in equal thirds', while A5 line 118 speaks of an 80-question 'reach-VIA' cell. If the cell is the thirds mix, the one-hop rule scores 2/3 and becomes the bar. The power figures themselves are arithmetically correct (reproduced exactly).

findings.problem: The sealed TEST_NEW set is not actually secret at 3-4 nodes. There are only 22 new shapes, and the design's own enumeration makes them public. The builder receives DEV_NEW (11), so TEST_NEW is exactly the other 11, whatever salt is used. At 5 nodes, the builder can equally train on all 227 non-DEV shapes. The only real protection is the non-isomorphism check against 'every world any training record carries'. But A2 runs that check 'before any use', when the split is built, and not on the submitted checkpoint's actual training inputs at evaluation.

At evaluation, run the two-method isomorphism check against TEST_NEW and fail closed on any match. Ban any training use of new shapes outside DEV_NEW as an explicit rule, not as a secret.

findings.problem: Helm reads node flags that leak the answer, and the design neither controls them nor registers a comparator for them. Helm reads is_declared_whole and the participant rank for every node. In the frozen bank, the VIA answer from the declared whole is the 'participant 2' node in 41 of 56 VIA questions, because every bank shape has the edge from labels[0] to labels[1]. The design does not say how declared_whole and the three primary labels are assigned in new-shape worlds. The source contract requires exactly 3 primary labels with whole = primary[0], so they must be assigned somehow. Assigned the training way, a flag rule ('answer VIA participant 2') could pass the reach cell without any structure. Assigned differently, the flags shift for new shapes only, which is a confound. A6 lists no flag-based comparator.

findings.problem: Using fresh declaration words would feed the domain, kind, function and setting signals through parts of Helm that were never trained. Helm maps each declaration token to a table row by its sorted position among the tokens present in that reading, not by a fixed vocabulary id. In the frozen bank, the domain field only ever had 4 distinct tokens, and setting only 12. Words outside the vocabulary are split into bytes: 'zorvic' becomes 6 byte ids, 101-124. Those byte ids sort below the word ids, so they take the low rows and push any familiar tokens to rows that were never used. The analogy family (the domain test and the same-domain decoy) and the definition/context controls would then mix structure with a broken input encoding. The node labels meanwhile are never read by Helm at all, only their sorted order. So 'overlap 0 for labels' tests nothing.

But a uniform shift can never reorder the worlds, so it can never separate the A7 witness pair, which needs different rankings. findings.problem:
Part B's wiring and matched-start rules conflict, and 'identical' is undefined.
(a) B1 requires PRESENT on FRESH containers. A new path whose output weights start at zero does not change any score at update 0, even though training can still flow through it. So it reads ABSENT or MIXED. The rule therefore forces random initialisation of the new path, which means the two arms already differ at update 0.
(b) Scoring the focus needs a wider world head, because the candidate input width is fixed. A widened (reshaped) tensor is not 'shared', so B3's bitwise rule does not cover it. The 'one change' then silently includes re-initialising the world head.
(c) 'Switch-OFF identical to the before-reading' is not checkable. The probe output contains source-file hashes (which must differ), container_kwargs, wall time and GPU telemetry.
